learning: Iteration 1 showed the 16 mm footprint helps the oval but leaves the s-bend and slalom losing the tape at the array edge, so the span is the next lever. The wider pitch reduces signal scale, so kp needs to rise to keep the same effective gain.
notes: Wider 32 mm sensor span at 16 mm footprints, with kp raised from 4.0 to 4.5 to offset the smaller signal per unit error on the wider pitch. Other controller settings are unchanged from iteration 1.
rationale: Iteration 1 is the best evidence so far. Going from 12 mm to 16 mm footprints cut oval line_loss from 0.95 to 0.45 and raised the oval finish rate to 0.9. The s-bend still loses the tape (line_loss 1.1, 16 of 20 off-track, max_error 0.056), and the slalom is still 0/20 with line_loss 1.05. rms_error stays low (0.017 and 0.022), so the robot is losing the tape at the edge of the array rather than tracking poorly. Following the Builder's intent, I keep the geometry unchanged here: sensor x at ±0.032, ±0.016, 0 on a 16 mm footprint, y 0.06, track 0.12, wheel 0.03, mass 0.8, body 0.16×0.12. The controller changes only because the wider pitch changes the signal scale. The weights [2,1,0,-1,-2] now correspond to 16 mm per unit instead of 12 mm, so the steering signal per unit of lateral error is about 25 percent smaller than in iteration 1. To keep the effective turn gain close to the iteration 1 setting, I raise kp from 4.0 to 4.5 and leave kd at 0.5 (the derivative term is already scaled with the signal, so it is not raised). ki stays at 0.1 and base_speed at 1.6, and line_loss stays 'last_direction', which has held the oval and bend tracks without controller errors. The expected effect is line_loss on the s-bend and slalom moving toward 0.5 or below, but I am not claiming an outcome for this candidate. Full measurements are requested so the next race can separate line loss, lookahead and oscillation effects.
